name: Riley
label: Ad-tolerant free-tier listener
who: I mostly use Spotify for free, and I accept ads and shuffle-only playback because the service is still useful to me. I would pay for Premium if I could choose songs and skip without ads, but I am not sure it is worth it yet.
value_for_money: Mixed: some say the free tier is enough if you just want playlists, while others say Premium is needed for choosing songs and skipping. The ad frequency on free is the main thing that makes them question the value.
loyalty: Keeps them on Spotify: free playlists and access to a large catalog. What would change things: more frustration with ads and shuffle-only free playback, which pushes some users toward Premium or alternatives like YouTube.
pain_points: Cannot skip or pick songs on free
Unclear when Premium features are active
likes: Ads are tolerable for background listening
reasons_to_stay: They stay on the free tier because they can listen to playlists and a large catalog without paying, and the ads are a trade-off they accept for background listening. They describe Premium as appealing mainly for choosing songs and avoiding ads.
tone: Frustrated but matter-of-fact, often describing how the free tier behaves in practice.
